## P4 - `linux.Start` re-disables TX offload on the `host`&#39;s `eth0` for host-networked `linux` nodes

**Location:** [nodes/linux/linux.go:102-116](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/nodes/linux/linux.go#L102-L116)

**Problem:** The new `Start` override skips the offload fix only when `ShouldSkipLifecycle()` returns true, which covers `IsRootNamespaceBased` kinds &#40;`host`, `ovs`, `bridge`&#41; and auto-remove nodes. A plain `linux` node with `network-mode: host` is not root-namespace-based, so `disableEth0TxOffload` runs `NSEthtoolTXOff(..., "eth0")` via `ExecFunction` in a network namespace that for `host` networking is the `host` namespace itself, disabling TX checksum offload on the `host`&#39;s `eth0`.

**Trigger:** `clab start`, `clab restart`, or an apply-driven restart &#40;see [`core/lifecycle.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/core/lifecycle.go#L1-L1)&#58;restartApplyNodes`) on a lab containing a `linux` node configured with `network-mode&#58; host&#96;.

**Impact:** The behavior already exists at deploy time in `PostDeploy`, so the failure mode is not new; this PR extends it so the `host` interface is touched again on every start cycle. In practice it re-applies an already-disabled setting, unless an operator deliberately re-enabled offload on the `host`, in which case it is silently turned off again. Marginal but real side effect on `host` state.

**Suggested correction:** Skip the fix when the node runs in `host` network mode, for example by returning early from `disableEth0TxOffload` when `n.Cfg.NetworkMode == "host"`, or at minimum document the limitation next to the `Start` override. The same reasoning applies to `iol.disableMgmtTxOffload` if desired, though IOL nodes are rarely used with `host` networking.


## P4 - No runnable check covers the `linux.Start` offload re-application

**Location:** [nodes/linux/linux.go:102-116](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/nodes/linux/linux.go#L102-L116)

**Problem:** The PR adds a stop/start regression test for the `cisco_iol` path in [`tests/10-basic-cisco_iol/01-iol.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/tests/10-basic-cisco_iol/01-iol.robot#L1-L1) but nothing exercises the identical [`linux.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/nodes/linux/linux.go#L1-L1) change. The existing smoke suite [`tests/01-smoke/28-node-lifecycle.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/tests/01-smoke/28-node-lifecycle.robot#L1-L1) runs stop/start/restart cycles on the `linux` nodes `l1`/`l2`, but only asserts dataplane ping, which does not regress when TX offload is enabled.

**Trigger:** Any future change that drops or breaks the `linux.Start` override.

**Impact:** The `linux` half of the fix ships without automated verification, so a future regression of the re-application on start would go unnoticed by CI.

**Suggested correction:** Add one assertion to [`tests/01-smoke/28-node-lifecycle.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/tests/01-smoke/28-node-lifecycle.robot#L1-L1) after a start cycle, for example `clab exec --node l1 --cmd "ethtool -k eth0"` asserting `tx-checksumming: off`. This fits the existing `clab exec` keyword style in that suite and requires no new lab.


## Coverage

- All four changed paths were reviewed&#58; [`nodes/iol/iol.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/nodes/iol/iol.go#L1-L1), [`nodes/linux/linux.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/nodes/linux/linux.go#L1-L1), [`tests/10-basic-cisco_iol/01-iol.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/tests/10-basic-cisco_iol/01-iol.robot#L1-L1), and [`docs/rn/0.81.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/docs/rn/0.81.md#L1-L1); base revisions of both Go files were compared and the helper extraction is behavior-preserving, including the macvlan guard.
- Verified that every container-runtime lifecycle path that recreates the mgmt veth routes through `Node.Start`&#58; [`core/start.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/core/start.go#L1-L1) &#40;`StartNodes`&#41;, [`core/restart.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/core/restart.go#L1-L1) &#40;`RestartNodes`&#41;, [`core/lifecycle.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/core/lifecycle.go#L1-L1)&#58;restartApplyNodes&#96;, and the start-existing-nodes path in [`core/deploy.go:672`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/core/deploy.go#L672-L672).
- Dataplane links restored by `RestoreEndpoints` reuse veths whose TX offload was disabled at creation time &#40;[`links/link_veth.go:206-249`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/links/link_veth.go#L206-L249)&#41;, so only the runtime-managed mgmt veth needs re-application; the PR scope is coherent.
- The c9s lab-runtime path &#40;[`core/labruntime.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/core/labruntime.go#L1-L1) -&#62; `LabRuntime.Start`&#41; does not invoke `Node.Start`, so the fix does not apply there; no evidence was found that this path recreates mgmt veths in the same way, so it is noted rather than flagged.
- The `iol` implementation matches the existing `sros.PostDeployEndpoints` precedent &#40;[`nodes/sros/sros.go:466-487`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/89be6648cb59ec135175fc697aed3b793f17bbfb/nodes/sros/sros.go#L466-L487)&#41;, including the macvlan guard and warn-and-continue failure handling; the near-duplication predates this PR and was not flagged.
- The release note wording &#39;management connectivity loss for `linux` nodes&#39; is broader than the code comment&#39;s stated symptom &#40;bridging/capture consumers on `eth0`&#41;, but it is defensible for `linux` nodes that `bridge` the mgmt interface, so it was not flagged.
- No tests or build commands were executed; the review is source-only and the new robot test was assessed statically. No topology-schema surface was touched, so no schema comparison was needed.

6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```

1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

79: 	r.Register(kindNames, func() clabnodes.Node {
80: 		return new(iol)

117: func (n *iol) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {
118: 	// Init DefaultNode
119: 	n.DefaultNode = *clabnodes.NewDefaultNode(n)
120: 	n.firstBoot = false
121: 
122: 	n.Cfg = cfg
123: 	for _, o := range opts {
124: 		o(n)
125: 	}
126: 
127: 	nodeType := strings.ToLower(n.Cfg.NodeType)
128: 
129: 	pid := n.Cfg.Index + 1 // n.Cfg.Index is zero-indexed, PID needs to be >= 1
130: 	if off := n.kindSpecificCfg().PidOffset; off != nil {
131: 		pid += *off
132: 	}
133: 
134: 	n.Pid = strconv.Itoa(pid)
135: 
136: 	env := map[string]string{
137: 		"IOL_PID": n.Pid,
138: 	}
139: 
140: 	n.Cfg.Env = clabutils.MergeStringMaps(env, n.Cfg.Env)
141: 
142: 	// check if user submitted node type is valid
143: 	switch nodeType {
144: 	case "":
145: 		n.isL2Node = strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(path.Base(n.Cfg.Image)), "l2")
146: 	case typeIOL:
147: 		n.isL2Node = false
148: 	case typeL2:
149: 		n.isL2Node = true
150: 	default:
151: 		return fmt.Errorf("invalid node type '%s'. Valid types are: %s",
152: 			n.Cfg.NodeType, strings.Join(validTypes, ", "))
153: 	}
154: 
155: 	if err := n.parseMgmtIntf(); err != nil {
156: 		return err
157: 	}
158: 
159: 	n.nvramFile = fmt.Sprint("nvram_", fmt.Sprintf("%05s", n.Pid))
160: 
161: 	n.Cfg.Binds = append(n.Cfg.Binds,
162: 		// mount nvram so that config persists
163: 		fmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, n.nvramFile), ":", path.Join(iol_workdir, n.nvramFile)),
164: 
165: 		// mount launch config
166: 		fmt.Sprint(filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, "boot_config.txt"), ":/iol/config.txt"),
167: 
168: 		// mount IOYAP and NETMAP for interface mapping
169: 		fmt.Sprint(filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, "iouyap.ini"), ":/iol/iouyap.ini"),
170: 		fmt.Sprint(filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, "NETMAP"), ":/iol/NETMAP"),
171: 	)
172: 
173: 	return nil
174: }

176: // parseMgmtIntf parses the mgmt-intf kind-specific config key and normalizes it to
177: // Ethernet<slot>/<port>;
178: // empty means the default Ethernet0/0.
179: func (n *iol) parseMgmtIntf() error {
180: 	if v := n.kindSpecificCfg().MgmtIntf; v != "" {
181: 		captureGroups, err := clabutils.GetRegexpCaptureGroups(CapturingIntfRegexp, v)
182: 		if err != nil {
183: 			return fmt.Errorf("invalid mgmt-intf %q: %w\n%s", v, err, IntfHelpMsg)
184: 		}
185: 
186: 		n.mgmtSlot, _ = strconv.Atoi(captureGroups["slot"])
187: 		n.mgmtPort, _ = strconv.Atoi(captureGroups["port"])
188: 
189: 		if n.mgmtSlot > 9 || n.mgmtPort > 3 {
190: 			return fmt.Errorf(
191: 				"invalid mgmt-intf %q: slot must be 0-9 and port must be 0-3", v)
192: 		}
193: 	}
194: 
195: 	n.mgmtIntf = fmt.Sprintf("Ethernet%d/%d", n.mgmtSlot, n.mgmtPort)
196: 	n.mgmtLinuxIdx = n.mgmtSlot*4 + n.mgmtPort
197: 
198: 	return nil
199: }
200: 
201: // swapMgmtIdx swaps linux interface index 0 with the management interface's index,
202: // so Ethernet0/0 takes the index a relocated management interface vacated.
203: func (n *iol) swapMgmtIdx(idx int) int {
204: 	switch idx {
205: 	case 0:
206: 		return n.mgmtLinuxIdx
207: 	case n.mgmtLinuxIdx:
208: 		return 0
209: 	}
210: 
211: 	return idx
212: }
213: 
214: // iolPortForLinuxIdx returns the IOL slot/port backed by linux interface index idx.
215: func (n *iol) iolPortForLinuxIdx(idx int) (slot, port int) {
216: 	mapped := n.swapMgmtIdx(idx)
217: 	return mapped / 4, mapped % 4
218: }
219: 
220: // ensureNumSlotsEnv exports CLAB_IOL_NUM_SLOTS when the management interface is
221: // relocated, so that its slot exists even when no link lands in it.
222: func (n *iol) ensureNumSlotsEnv() {
223: 	if n.mgmtLinuxIdx == 0 || n.Cfg.Env["CLAB_IOL_NUM_SLOTS"] != "" {
224: 		return
225: 	}
226: 
227: 	intfIdxRegexp := regexp.MustCompile(`\d+`)
228: 	needed := n.mgmtSlot + 1
229: 
230: 	for _, ep := range n.Endpoints {
231: 		x, _ := strconv.Atoi(intfIdxRegexp.FindString(ep.GetIfaceName()))
232: 		if slot, _ := n.iolPortForLinuxIdx(x); slot+1 > needed {
233: 			needed = slot + 1
234: 		}
235: 	}
236: 
237: 	n.Cfg.Env["CLAB_IOL_NUM_SLOTS"] = strconv.Itoa(needed)
238: }

240: func (n *iol) PreDeploy(ctx context.Context, params *clabnodes.PreDeployParams) error {
241: 	clabutils.CreateDirectory(n.Cfg.LabDir, clabconstants.PermissionsOpen)
242: 
243: 	if v := n.kindSpecificCfg().BootstrapConfig; v != "" {
244: 		switch p := clabutils.ResolvePath(v, params.TopoPaths.TopologyFileDir()); {
245: 		case strings.EqualFold(v, "none"):
246: 			n.bootstrapNone = true
247: 		case clabutils.FileExists(p):
248: 			n.bootstrapCfgFile = p
249: 		default:
250: 			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap-config file %q does not exist", p)
251: 		}
252: 	}
253: 
254: 	_, err := n.LoadOrGenerateCertificate(params.Cert, params.TopologyName)
255: 	if err != nil {
256: 		return err
257: 	}
258: 
259: 	n.ensureNumSlotsEnv()
260: 
261: 	return n.CreateIOLFiles(ctx)
262: }
263: 
264: func (n *iol) PostDeploy(ctx context.Context, _ *clabnodes.PostDeployParams) error {
265: 	log.Infof("Running postdeploy actions for Cisco IOL '%s' node", n.Cfg.ShortName)
266: 
267: 	n.disableMgmtTxOffload(ctx)
268: 
269: 	if err := n.GenBootConfig(ctx); err != nil {
270: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate boot config: %w", err)
271: 	}
272: 
273: 	// Must update mgmt IP if not first boot, unless the node boots without a baseline config
274: 	if !n.firstBoot && !n.bootstrapNone {
275: 		return n.UpdateMgmtIntf(ctx)
276: 	}
277: 
278: 	return nil
279: }

281: // Start re-applies the mgmt veth TX offload fix after a stop/start cycle. The runtime
282: // recreates the mgmt veth (it is never parked), so its offload settings reset to defaults.
283: // See disableMgmtTxOffload for why IOL cannot function with it enabled.
284: func (n *iol) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
285: 	if err := n.DefaultNode.Start(ctx); err != nil {
286: 		return err
287: 	}
288: 
289: 	// DefaultNode.Start no-ops for root-ns and auto-remove nodes; skip the offload fix
290: 	// for them as well, as there is no container mgmt veth to adjust.
291: 	if n.ShouldSkipLifecycle() {
292: 		return nil
293: 	}
294: 
295: 	n.disableMgmtTxOffload(ctx)
296: 
297: 	return nil
298: }
299: 
300: // disableMgmtTxOffload disables TX checksum offload on the host NS veth for the mgmt interface.
301: // iouyap bridges IOL interfaces over packet sockets; frames carrying an offloaded
302: // (CHECKSUM_PARTIAL) checksum reach the IOL process with an incomplete checksum, which its
303: // TCP/IP stack drops, breaking TCP/UDP connectivity.
304: func (n *iol) disableMgmtTxOffload(ctx context.Context) {
305: 	if n.Runtime.Mgmt().Driver == clabtypes.MgmtDriverMacvlan {
306: 		return
307: 	}
308: 
309: 	var peerIfIndex int
310: 	err := n.ExecFunction(ctx, clabutils.VethPeerIndex("eth0", &peerIfIndex))
311: 	if err != nil {
312: 		log.Warn("Failed to get veth peer index for IOL mgmt interface",
313: 			"node", n.Cfg.ShortName,
314: 			"error", err)
315: 		return
316: 	}
317: 
318: 	if err := clabutils.DisableTxOffloadByIndex(peerIfIndex); err != nil {
319: 		log.Warn("Failed to disable TX checksum offload on IOL mgmt host veth",
320: 			"node", n.Cfg.ShortName,
321: 			"error", err)
322: 	}
323: }
324: 
325: func (n *iol) CreateIOLFiles(ctx context.Context) error {
326: 	// If NVRAM already exists, don't need to create
327: 	// otherwise saved configs in NVRAM are overwritten.
328: 	if !clabutils.FileExists(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, n.nvramFile)) {
329: 		// create nvram file
330: 		clabutils.CreateFile(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, n.nvramFile), "")
331: 		n.firstBoot = true
332: 	}
333: 
334: 	// create these files so the bind monut doesn't automatically
335: 	// make folders.
336: 	clabutils.CreateFile(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, "boot_config.txt"), "")
337: 
338: 	return n.GenInterfaceConfig(ctx)
339: }

341: // Generate interfaces configuration for IOL (and iouyap/netmap).
342: func (n *iol) GenInterfaceConfig(_ context.Context) error {
343: 	// add 'boilerplate' to NETMAP and iouyap.ini for the management port
344: 	iouyapData := fmt.Sprintf(
345: 		"[default]\nbase_port = 49000\nnetmap = /iol/NETMAP\n[513:%d/%d]\neth_dev = eth0\n",
346: 		n.mgmtSlot,
347: 		n.mgmtPort,
348: 	)
349: 	netmapdata := fmt.Sprintf(
350: 		"%s:%d/%d 513:%d/%d\n",
351: 		n.Pid,
352: 		n.mgmtSlot,
353: 		n.mgmtPort,
354: 		n.mgmtSlot,
355: 		n.mgmtPort,
356: 	)
357: 
358: 	slot, port := 0, 0
359: 
360: 	// Regexp to pull number out of linux'ethX' interface naming
361: 	IntfRegExpr := regexp.MustCompile(`\d+`)
362: 
363: 	for _, intf := range n.Endpoints {
364: 		// get numeric interface number and cast to int
365: 		x, _ := strconv.Atoi(IntfRegExpr.FindString(intf.GetIfaceName()))
366: 
367: 		// Interface naming is Ethernet{slot}/{port}. Each slot contains max 4 ports
368: 		slot, port = n.iolPortForLinuxIdx(x)
369: 
370: 		// append data to write to NETMAP and IOUYAP files
371: 		iouyapData += fmt.Sprintf("[513:%d/%d]\neth_dev = %s\n", slot, port, intf.GetIfaceName())
372: 		netmapdata += fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d/%d 513:%d/%d\n", n.Pid, slot, port, slot, port)
373: 
374: 		// populate template array for config
375: 		ipv4Addr := ""
376: 		ipv4Mask := ""
377: 		v4Prefix := intf.GetIPv4Addr()
378: 		ipv6Addr := ""
379: 
380: 		if v4Prefix.IsValid() {
381: 			ipv4Addr = v4Prefix.Addr().String()
382: 			ipv4Mask = clabutils.CIDRToDDN(v4Prefix.Bits())
383: 		}
384: 
385: 		if a := intf.GetIPv6Addr(); a.IsValid() {
386: 			ipv6Addr = a.String()
387: 		}
388: 
389: 		n.interfaces = append(n.interfaces,
390: 			IOLInterface{
391: 				IfaceName: intf.GetIfaceName(),
392: 				IfaceIdx:  x,
393: 				Slot:      slot,
394: 				Port:      port,
395: 				IPv4Addr:  ipv4Addr,
396: 				IPv4Mask:  ipv4Mask,
397: 				IPv6Addr:  ipv6Addr,
398: 			},
399: 		)
400: 	}
401: 
402: 	// create IOUYAP and NETMAP file for interface mappings
403: 	err := clabutils.CreateFile(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, "iouyap.ini"), iouyapData)
404: 	if err != nil {
405: 		return err
406: 	}
407: 	err = clabutils.CreateFile(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, "NETMAP"), netmapdata)
408: 
409: 	return err
410: }

412: func (n *iol) GenBootConfig(_ context.Context) error {
413: 	n.bootCfg = cfgTemplate
414: 
415: 	switch {
416: 	case n.bootstrapNone:
417: 		n.bootCfg = "{{ .PartialCfg }}"
418: 	case n.bootstrapCfgFile != "":
419: 		cfg, err := os.ReadFile(n.bootstrapCfgFile)
420: 		if err != nil {
421: 			return err
422: 		}
423: 
424: 		n.bootCfg = string(cfg)
425: 	}
426: 
427: 	if n.Cfg.StartupConfig != "" {
428: 		cfg, err := os.ReadFile(n.Cfg.StartupConfig)
429: 		if err != nil {
430: 			return err
431: 		}
432: 
433: 		if clabutils.IsPartialConfigFile(n.Cfg.StartupConfig) {
434: 			n.partialStartupCfg = string(cfg)
435: 		} else {
436: 			n.bootCfg = string(cfg)
437: 		}
438: 	}
439: 
440: 	// create startup config template
441: 	tpl := IOLTemplateData{
442: 		Hostname:           n.Cfg.ShortName,
443: 		IsL2Node:           n.isL2Node,
444: 		MgmtIntf:           n.mgmtIntf,
445: 		MgmtIPv4Addr:       n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4Address,
446: 		MgmtIPv4SubnetMask: clabutils.CIDRToDDN(n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4PrefixLength),
447: 		MgmtIPv4GW:         n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4Gateway,
448: 		MgmtIPv6Addr:       n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6Address,
449: 		MgmtIPv6PrefixLen:  n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6PrefixLength,
450: 		MgmtIPv6GW:         n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6Gateway,
451: 		DataIFaces:         n.interfaces,
452: 	}
453: 
454: 	// render the partial startup config so template variables work in partials too
455: 	if n.partialStartupCfg != "" {
456: 		partialTpl, err := template.New("clab-iol-partial-config").Funcs(
457: 			clabutils.CreateFuncs()).Parse(n.partialStartupCfg)
458: 		if err != nil {
459: 			return err
460: 		}
461: 
462: 		buf := new(bytes.Buffer)
463: 		if err := partialTpl.Execute(buf, tpl); err != nil {
464: 			return err
465: 		}
466: 
467: 		tpl.PartialCfg = buf.String()
468: 	}
469: 
470: 	IOLCfgTpl, err := template.New("clab-iol-default-config").Funcs(
471: 		clabutils.CreateFuncs()).Parse(n.bootCfg)
472: 	if err != nil {
473: 		return err
474: 	}
475: 
476: 	// generate the config
477: 	buf := new(bytes.Buffer)
478: 	err = IOLCfgTpl.Execute(buf, tpl)
479: 	if err != nil {
480: 		return err
481: 	}
482: 
483: 	return clabutils.CreateFile(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, "boot_config.txt"), buf.String())
484: }
485: 
486: type IOLTemplateData struct {
487: 	Hostname           string
488: 	IsL2Node           bool
489: 	MgmtIntf           string
490: 	MgmtIPv4Addr       string
491: 	MgmtIPv4SubnetMask string
492: 	MgmtIPv4GW         string
493: 	MgmtIPv6Addr       string
494: 	MgmtIPv6PrefixLen  int
495: 	MgmtIPv6GW         string
496: 	DataIFaces         []IOLInterface
497: 	PartialCfg         string
498: }

500: // IOLInterface struct stores mapping info between
501: // IOL interface name and linux container interface.
502: type IOLInterface struct {
503: 	IfaceName string
504: 	IfaceIdx  int
505: 	Slot      int
506: 	Port      int
507: 	IPv4Addr  string
508: 	IPv4Mask  string
509: 	IPv6Addr  string
510: }
511: 
512: func (n *iol) GetMappedInterfaceName(ifName string) (string, error) {
513: 	captureGroups, err := clabutils.GetRegexpCaptureGroups(CapturingIntfRegexp, ifName)
514: 	if err != nil {
515: 		return "", err
516: 	}
517: 
518: 	indexGroups := []string{"slot", "port"}
519: 	parsedIndices := make(map[string]int)
520: 	foundIndices := make(map[string]bool)
521: 
522: 	for _, indexKey := range indexGroups {
523: 		if index, found := captureGroups[indexKey]; found && index != "" {
524: 			foundIndices[indexKey] = true
525: 			parsedIndices[indexKey], err = strconv.Atoi(index)
526: 			if err != nil {
527: 				return "", fmt.Errorf(
528: 					"%q parsed %s index %q could not be cast to an integer",
529: 					ifName,
530: 					indexKey,
531: 					index,
532: 				)
533: 			}
534: 			if parsedIndices[indexKey] < 0 {
535: 				return "", fmt.Errorf(
536: 					"%q parsed %q index %q does not match requirement >= 0",
537: 					ifName,
538: 					indexKey,
539: 					index,
540: 				)
541: 			}
542: 		} else {
543: 			foundIndices[indexKey] = false
544: 		}
545: 	}
546: 
547: 	// return an ethX interface name. Slots are in 'groups' of 4 interfaces each
548: 	if foundIndices["slot"] && foundIndices["port"] {
549: 		idx := n.swapMgmtIdx((parsedIndices["slot"] * 4) + parsedIndices["port"])
550: 		return fmt.Sprintf("eth%d", idx), nil
551: 	} else {
552: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("%q missing slot or port index", ifName)
553: 	}
554: }

556: // AddEndpoint override maps the endpoint name to an ethX-based naming where necessary, before
557: // adding it to the node endpoints. Returns an error if the mapping goes wrong or if the
558: // interface name is NOT allowed.
559: func (n *iol) AddEndpoint(e clablinks.Endpoint) error {
560: 	endpointName := e.GetIfaceName()
561: 	var IFaceName, IFaceAlias string
562: 
563: 	IFaceName = endpointName
564: 
565: 	if !(DefaultIntfRegexp.MatchString(endpointName)) &&
566: 		AllowedIntfRegexp.MatchString(endpointName) {
567: 		log.Debugf("%s: %s needs mapping", n.Cfg.ShortName, endpointName)
568: 		mappedName, err := n.GetMappedInterfaceName(endpointName)
569: 		if err != nil {
570: 			return fmt.Errorf(
571: 				"%q interface name %q could not be mapped to an ethX-based interface name: %w\n%s",
572: 				n.Cfg.ShortName,
573: 				e.GetIfaceName(),
574: 				err,
575: 				IntfHelpMsg,
576: 			)
577: 		}
578: 		log.Debugf(
579: 			"Interface Mapping: Mapping interface %q (ifAlias) to %q (ifName)",
580: 			endpointName,
581: 			mappedName,
582: 		)
583: 		IFaceName = mappedName
584: 		IFaceAlias = endpointName
585: 	}
586: 
587: 	e.SetIfaceName(IFaceName)
588: 	// should be nil if ethX naming is used.
589: 	e.SetIfaceAlias(IFaceAlias)
590: 	n.Endpoints = append(n.Endpoints, e)
591: 
592: 	return nil
593: }

595: func (n *iol) CheckInterfaceName() error {
596: 	err := n.CheckInterfaceOverlap()
597: 	if err != nil {
598: 		return err
599: 	}
600: 
601: 	for _, e := range n.Endpoints {
602: 		IFaceName := e.GetIfaceName()
603: 		// eth0 always backs the management interface
604: 		if IFaceName == "eth0" {
605: 			return fmt.Errorf(
606: 				"IOL Node: %q. Management interface %s (eth0) is not allowed",
607: 				n.Cfg.ShortName,
608: 				n.mgmtIntf,
609: 			)
610: 		}
611: 
612: 		if !DefaultIntfRegexp.MatchString(IFaceName) {
613: 			return fmt.Errorf(
614: 				"IOL Node %q has an interface named %q which doesn't match the required pattern. %s",
615: 				n.Cfg.ShortName,
616: 				IFaceName,
617: 				IntfHelpMsg,
618: 			)
619: 		}
620: 	}
621: 
622: 	return nil
623: }

625: func (n *iol) UpdateMgmtIntf(ctx context.Context) error {
626: 	// L2 IOL images default to switchport mode, which rejects IP addresses.
627: 	switchportCmd := ""
628: 	if n.isL2Node {
629: 		switchportCmd = "no switchport\r"
630: 	}
631: 
632: 	waitCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, bootPromptTimeout)
633: 	defer cancel()
634: 
635: 	// 1. Start streaming container logs
636: 	logReader, err := n.Runtime.StreamLogs(waitCtx, n.Cfg.LongName)
637: 	if err != nil {
638: 		log.Warn("Skipping IOL mgmt interface update, cannot stream container logs",
639: 			"node", n.Cfg.ShortName, "error", err)
640: 		return nil
641: 	}
642: 	defer logReader.Close()
643: 
644: 	// Ticker to periodically send carriage returns (\r) to wake up the serial console
645: 	ticker := time.NewTicker(2 * time.Second)
646: 	defer ticker.Stop()
647: 
648: 	// Scanner to read the container log output line by line
649: 	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(logReader)
650: 
651: 	// Asynchronously send carriage returns since scanner.Scan() blocks
652: 	tickCtx, stopTicker := context.WithCancel(waitCtx)
653: 	defer stopTicker()
654: 	tickerDone := make(chan struct{})
655: 
656: 	go func() {
657: 		defer close(tickerDone)
658: 		for {
659: 			select {
660: 			case <-tickCtx.Done():
661: 				return
662: 			case <-ticker.C:
663: 				_ = n.Runtime.WriteToStdinNoWait(tickCtx, n.Cfg.LongName, []byte("\r"))
664: 			}
665: 		}
666: 	}()
667: 
668: 	bootComplete := false
669: 	for scanner.Scan() {
670: 		// Trim control characters and spaces from the log line
671: 		line := strings.TrimSpace(scanner.Text())
672: 		if line == "" {
673: 			continue
674: 		}
675: 
676: 		log.Debugf("[IOL Boot Log] %s", line)
677: 
678: 		// Match boot prompts (>, #, or initial config dialog)
679: 		if strings.HasSuffix(line, ">") ||
680: 			strings.HasSuffix(line, "#") ||
681: 			strings.Contains(line, "initial configuration dialog?") {
682: 
683: 			// Ignore syslog messages containing '>'
684: 			if strings.Contains(line, "%") {
685: 				continue
686: 			}
687: 
688: 			log.Infof("IOL boot prompt detected (%s). Proceeding with configuration.", line)
689: 			bootComplete = true
690: 			break
691: 		}
692: 	}
693: 
694: 	stopTicker()
695: 	<-tickerDone
696: 
697: 	if !bootComplete {
698: 		if ctx.Err() != nil {
699: 			return ctx.Err()
700: 		}
701: 		if waitCtx.Err() != nil {
702: 			return fmt.Errorf("node %q: timed out after %s waiting for IOL boot prompt",
703: 				n.Cfg.ShortName, bootPromptTimeout)
704: 		}
705: 		if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
706: 			return fmt.Errorf("error reading IOL log stream: %w", err)
707: 		}
708: 	}
709: 	// --- End of prompt detection ---
710: 
711: 	// All IOS commands applied here are idempotent and safe to re-run.
712: 	mgmt_str := fmt.Sprintf(
713: 		"\rend\renable\rconfig terminal\rinterface %s\r%sip address %s %s\rno ipv6 address\ripv6 address %s/%d\rexit\rip route vrf clab-mgmt 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 %s %s\ripv6 route vrf clab-mgmt ::/0 %s %s\rend\rwr\r",
714: 		n.mgmtIntf,
715: 		switchportCmd,
716: 		n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4Address,
717: 		clabutils.CIDRToDDN(n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4PrefixLength),
718: 		n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6Address,
719: 		n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6PrefixLength,
720: 		n.mgmtIntf,
721: 		n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4Gateway,
722: 		n.mgmtIntf,
723: 		n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6Gateway,
724: 	)
725: 	data := []byte(mgmt_str)
726: 
727: 	var lastErr error
728: 	for i := range 3 {
729: 		if i > 0 {
730: 			time.Sleep(10 * time.Second)
731: 		}
732: 		lastErr = n.Runtime.WriteToStdinNoWait(ctx, n.Cfg.ContainerID, data)
733: 		if lastErr == nil {
734: 			break
735: 		}
736: 		log.Warnf("UpdateMgmtIntf: attempt %d/3 failed for %s: %v",
737: 			i+1, n.Cfg.ShortName, lastErr)
738: 	}
739: 	return lastErr
740: }

742: // SaveConfig is used for "clab save" functionality -- it saves the running config to the startup
743: // configuration.
744: func (n *iol) SaveConfig(_ context.Context) (*clabnodes.SaveConfigResult, error) {
745: 	p, err := platform.NewPlatform(
746: 		"cisco_iosxe",
747: 		n.Cfg.LongName,
748: 		options.WithAuthNoStrictKey(),
749: 		options.WithAuthUsername(n.Cfg.Credentials.Username),
750: 		options.WithAuthPassword(n.Cfg.Credentials.Password),
751: 	)
752: 	if err != nil {
753: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create platform; error: %+v", err)
754: 	}
755: 
756: 	d, err := p.GetNetworkDriver()
757: 	if err != nil {
758: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to fetch network driver from the platform; error: %+v", err)
759: 	}
760: 
761: 	err = d.Open()
762: 	if err != nil {
763: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open driver; error: %+v", err)
764: 	}
765: 
766: 	defer d.Close()
767: 
768: 	_, err = d.SendCommand("write memory")
769: 	if err != nil {
770: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to send command; error: %+v", err)
771: 	}
772: 
773: 	log.Infof(
774: 		"Successfully copied running configuration to startup configuration file for node: %q\n",
775: 		n.Cfg.ShortName,
776: 	)
777: 	return nil, nil
778: }

The runtime\n282: // recreates the mgmt veth (it is never parked), so its offload settings reset to defaults.\n283: // See disableMgmtTxOffload for why IOL cannot function with it enabled.\n284: func (n *iol) Start(ctx context.Context) error {\n285: \tif err := n.DefaultNode.Start(ctx); err != nil {\n286: \t\treturn err\n287: \t}\n288: \n289: \t// DefaultNode.Start no-ops for root-ns and auto-remove nodes; skip the offload fix\n290: \t// for them as well, as there is no container mgmt veth to adjust.\n291: \tif n.ShouldSkipLifecycle() {\n292: \t\treturn nil\n293: \t}\n294: \n295: \tn.disableMgmtTxOffload(ctx)\n296: \n297: \treturn nil\n298: }\n299: \n300: // disableMgmtTxOffload disables TX checksum offload on the host NS veth for the mgmt interface.\n301: // iouyap bridges IOL interfaces over packet sockets; frames carrying an offloaded\n302: // (CHECKSUM_PARTIAL) checksum reach the IOL process with an incomplete checksum, which its\n303: // TCP/IP stack drops, breaking TCP/UDP connectivity.\n304: func (n *iol) disableMgmtTxOffload(ctx context.Context) {\n305: \tif n.Runtime.Mgmt().Driver == clabtypes.MgmtDriverMacvlan {\n306: \t\treturn\n307: \t}\n308: \n309: \tvar peerIfIndex int\n310: \terr := n.ExecFunction(ctx, clabutils.VethPeerIndex(\"eth0\", &peerIfIndex))\n311: \tif err != nil {\n312: \t\tlog.Warn(\"Failed to get veth peer index for IOL mgmt interface\",\n313: \t\t\t\"node\", n.Cfg.ShortName,\n314: \t\t\t\"error\", err)\n315: \t\treturn\n316: \t}\n317: \n318: \tif err := clabutils.DisableTxOffloadByIndex(peerIfIndex); err != nil {\n319: \t\tlog.Warn(\"Failed to disable TX checksum offload on IOL mgmt host veth\",\n320: \t\t\t\"node\", n.Cfg.ShortName,\n321: \t\t\t\"error\", err)\n322: \t}\n323: }\n324: \n325: func (n *iol) CreateIOLFiles(ctx context.Context) error {\n326: \t// If NVRAM already exists, don't need to create\n327: \t// otherwise saved configs in NVRAM are overwritten.\n328: \tif !clabutils.FileExists(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, n.nvramFile)) {\n329: \t\t// create nvram file\n330: \t\tclabutils.CreateFile(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, n.nvramFile), \"\")\n331: \t\tn.firstBoot = true\n332: \t}\n333: \n334: \t// create these files so the bind monut doesn't automatically\n335: \t// make folders.\n336: \tclabutils.CreateFile(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, \"boot_config.txt\"), \"\")\n337: \n338: \treturn n.GenInterfaceConfig(ctx)\n339: }\n340: \n341: // Generate interfaces configuration for IOL (and iouyap/netmap).\n342: func (n *iol) GenInterfaceConfig(_ context.Context) error {\n343: \t// add 'boilerplate' to NETMAP and iouyap.ini for the management port\n344: \tiouyapData := fmt.Sprintf(\n345: \t\t\"[default]\\nbase_port = 49000\\nnetmap = /iol/NETMAP\\n[513:%d/%d]\\neth_dev = eth0\\n\",\n346: \t\tn.mgmtSlot,\n347: \t\tn.mgmtPort,\n348: \t)\n349: \tnetmapdata := fmt.Sprintf(\n350: \t\t\"%s:%d/%d 513:%d/%d\\n\",\n351: \t\tn.Pid,\n352: \t\tn.mgmtSlot,\n353: \t\tn.mgmtPort,\n354: \t\tn.mgmtSlot,\n355: \t\tn.mgmtPort,\n356: \t)\n357: \n358: \tslot, port := 0, 0\n359: \n360: \t// Regexp to pull number out of linux'ethX' interface naming\n361: \tIntfRegExpr := regexp.MustCompile(`\\d+`)\n362: \n363: \tfor _, intf := range n.Endpoints {\n364: \t\t// get numeric interface number and cast to int\n365: \t\tx, _ := strconv.Atoi(IntfRegExpr.FindString(intf.GetIfaceName()))\n366: \n367: \t\t// Interface naming is Ethernet{slot}/{port}. Each slot contains max 4 ports\n368: \t\tslot, port = n.iolPortForLinuxIdx(x)\n369: \n370: \t\t// append data to write to NETMAP and IOUYAP files\n371: \t\tiouyapData += fmt.Sprintf(\"[513:%d/%d]\\neth_dev = %s\\n\", slot, port, intf.GetIfaceName())\n372: \t\tnetmapdata += fmt.Sprintf(\"%s:%d/%d 513:%d/%d\\n\", n.Pid, slot, port, slot, port)\n373: \n374: \t\t// populate template array for config\n375: \t\tipv4Addr := \"\"\n376: \t\tipv4Mask := \"\"\n377: \t\tv4Prefix := intf.GetIPv4Addr()\n378: \t\tipv6Addr := \"\"\n379: \n380: \t\tif v4Prefix.IsValid() \t\t\tipv6Addr = a.String()\n387: \t\t}\n388: \n389: \t\tn.interfaces = append(n.interfaces,\n390: \t\t\tIOLInterface{\n391: \t\t\t\tIfaceName: intf.GetIfaceName(),\n392: \t\t\t\tIfaceIdx:  x,\n393: \t\t\t\tSlot:      slot,\n394: \t\t\t\tPort:      port,\n395: \t\t\t\tIPv4Addr:  ipv4Addr,\n396: \t\t\t\tIPv4Mask:  ipv4Mask,\n397: \t\t\t\tIPv6Addr:  ipv6Addr,\n398: \t\t\t},\n399: \t\t)\n400: \t}\n401: \n402: \t// create IOUYAP and NETMAP file for interface mappings\n403: \terr := clabutils.CreateFile(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, \"iouyap.ini\"), iouyapData)\n404: \tif err != nil {\n405: \t\treturn err\n406: \t}\n407: \terr = clabutils.CreateFile(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, \"NETMAP\"), netmapdata)\n408: \n409: \treturn err\n410: }\n411: \n412: func (n *iol) GenBootConfig(_ context.Context) error {\n413: \tn.bootCfg = cfgTemplate\n414: \n415: \tswitch {\n416: \tcase n.bootstrapNone:\n417: \t\tn.bootCfg = \"{{ .PartialCfg }}\"\n418: \tcase n.bootstrapCfgFile != \"\":\n419: \t\tcfg, err := os.ReadFile(n.bootstrapCfgFile)\n420: \t\tif err != nil {\n421: \t\t\treturn err\n422: \t\t}\n423: \n424: \t\tn.bootCfg = string(cfg)\n425: \t}\n426: \n427: \tif n.Cfg.StartupConfig != \"\" {\n428: \t\tcfg, err := os.ReadFile(n.Cfg.StartupConfig)\n429: \t\tif err != nil {\n430: \t\t\treturn err\n431: \t\t}\n432: \n433: \t\tif clabutils.IsPartialConfigFile(n.Cfg.StartupConfig) {\n434: \t\t\tn.partialStartupCfg = string(cfg)\n435: \t\t} else {\n436: \t\t\tn.bootCfg = string(cfg)\n437: \t\t}\n438: \t}\n439: \n440: \t// create startup config template\n441: \ttpl := IOLTemplateData{\n442: \t\tHostname:           n.Cfg.ShortName,\n443: \t\tIsL2Node:           n.isL2Node,\n444: \t\tMgmtIntf:           n.mgmtIntf,\n445: n.interfaces,\n452: \t}\n453: \n454: \t// render the partial startup config so template variables work in partials too\n455: \tif n.partialStartupCfg != \"\" {\n456: \t\tpartialTpl, err := new(bytes.Buffer)\n463: \t\tif err := partialTpl.Execute(buf, tpl); err != nil {\n464: \t\t\treturn err\n465: \t\t}\n466: \n467: \t\ttpl.PartialCfg = buf.String()\n468: \t}\n469: \n470: \tIOLCfgTpl, err := template.New(\"clab-iol-default-config\").Funcs(\n471: \t\tclabutils.CreateFuncs()).Parse(n.bootCfg)\n472: \tif err != nil {\n473: \t\treturn err\n474: \t}\n475: \n476: \t// generate the config\n477: \tbuf := new(bytes.Buffer)\n478: \terr = IOLCfgTpl.Execute(buf, tpl)\n479: \tif err != nil {\n480: \t\treturn err\n481: \t}\n482: \n483: \treturn clabutils.CreateFile(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, \"boot_config.txt\"), buf.String())\n484: }\n485: \n486: type IOLTemplateData struct {\n487: \tHostname           string\n488: \tIsL2Node           bool\n489: \tMgmtIntf           string\n490: \tMgmtIPv4Addr       string\n491: \tMgmtIPv4SubnetMask string\n492: \tMgmtIPv4GW         string\n493: \tMgmtIPv6Addr       string\n494: \tMgmtIPv6PrefixLen interface name and linux container interface.\n502: type IOLInterface struct {\n503: \tIfaceName string\n504: \tIfaceIdx  int\n505: \tSlot      int\n506: \tPort      int\n507: \tIPv4Addr  string\n508: \tIPv4Mask  string\n509: \tIPv6Addr  string\n510: }\n511: \n512: func (n *iol) GetMappedInterfaceName(ifName string) (string, error) {\n513: \tcaptureGroups, err := clabutils.GetRegexpCaptureGroups(CapturingIntfRegexp, ifName)\n514: \tif err != nil {\n515: \t\treturn \"\", err\n516: \t}\n517: \n518: \tindexGroups := []string{\"slot\", \"port\"}\n519: \tparsedIndices := make(map[string]int)\n520: \tfoundIndices := make(map[string]bool)\n521: \n522: \tfor _, indexKey := range indexGroups {\n523: \t\tif index, found := captureGroups[indexKey]; found && index != \"\" {\n524: \t\t\tfoundIndices[indexKey] = true\n525: \t\t\tparsedIndices[indexKey], err = strconv.Atoi(index)\n526: \t\t\tif err != nil {\n527: \t\t\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\n528: \t\t\t\t\t\"%q parsed %s index %q could not be cast to an integer\",\n529: \t\t\t\t\tifName,\n530: \t\t\t\t\tindexKey,\n531: \t\t\t\t\tindex,\n532: \t\t\t\t)\n533: \t\t\t}\n534: \t\t\tif parsedIndices[indexKey] < 0 {\n535: \t\t\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\n536: \t\t\t\t\t\"%q parsed %q index %q does not match requirement >= 0\",\n537: \t\t\t\t\tifName,\n538: \t\t\t\t\tindexKey,\n539: \t\t\t\t\tindex,\n540: \t\t\t\t)\n541: \t\t\t}\n542: \t\t} else {\n543: \t\t\tfoundIndices[indexKey] = false\n544: \t\t}\n545: \t}\n546: \n547: \t// return an ethX interface name. Slots are in 'groups' of 4 interfaces each\n548: \tif foundIndices[\"slot\"] && foundIndices[\"port\"] {\n549: \t\tidx := n.swapMgmtIdx((parsedIndices[\"slot\"] * 4) + parsedIndices[\"port\"])\n550: \t\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"eth%d\", idx), nil\n551: \t} else {\n552: \t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"%q missing slot or port index\", ifName)\n553: \t}\n554: }\n555: \n556: // AddEndpoint override maps the endpoint name to an ethX-based naming where necessary, before\n557: // adding it to the node endpoints. Returns an error if the mapping goes wrong or if the\n558: // interface name is NOT allowed.\n559: func (n *iol) AddEndpoint(e clablinks.Endpoint) error {\n560: \tendpointName := e.GetIfaceName()\n561: \tvar IFaceName, IFaceAlias string\n562: \n563: \tIFaceName = endpointName\n564: \n565: \tif !(DefaultIntfRegexp.MatchString(endpointName)) &&\n566: \t\tAllowedIntfRegexp.MatchString(endpointName) {\n567: \t\tlog.Debugf(\"%s: %s needs mapping\", n.Cfg.ShortName, endpointName)\n568: \t\tmappedName, err := n.GetMappedInterfaceName(endpointName)\n569: \t\tif err != nil {\n570: \t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\n571: \t\t\t\t\"%q interface name %q could not be mapped to an ethX-based interface name: %w\\n%s\",\n572: \t\t\t\tn.Cfg.ShortName,\n573: \t\t\t\te.GetIfaceName(),\n574: \t\t\t\terr,\n575: \t\t\t\tIntfHelpMsg,\n576: \t\t\t)\n577: \t\t}\n578: \t\tlog.Debugf(\n579: \t\t\t\"Interface Mapping: Mapping interface %q (ifAlias) to %q (ifName)\",\n580: \t\t\tendpointName,\n581: \t\t\tmappedName,\n582: \t\t)\n583: \t\tIFaceName = mappedName\n584: \t\tIFaceAlias = endpointName\n585: \t}\n586: \n587: \te.SetIfaceName(IFaceName)\n588: \t// should be nil if ethX naming is used.\n589: \te.SetIfaceAlias(IFaceAlias)\n590: \tn.Endpoints = append(n.Endpoints, e)\n591: \n592: \treturn nil\n593: }\n594: \n595: func (n *iol) CheckInterfaceName() error {\n596: \terr := n.CheckInterfaceOverlap()\n597: \tif err != nil {\n598: \t\treturn err\n599: \t}\n600: \n601: \tfor _, e := range n.Endpoints {\n602: \t\tIFaceName := e.GetIfaceName()\n603: \t\t// eth0 always backs the management interface\n604: \t\tif IFaceName == \"eth0\" {\n605: \t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\n606: \t\t\t\t\"IOL Node: %q. Management interface %s (eth0) is not allowed\",\n607: \t\t\t\tn.Cfg.ShortName,\n608: \t\t\t\tn.mgmtIntf,\n609: \t\t\t)\n610: \t\t}\n611: \n612: \t\tif !DefaultIntfRegexp.MatchString(IFaceName) {\n613: \t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\n614: \t\t\t\t\"IOL Node %q has an interface named %q which doesn't match the required pattern. %s\",\n615: \t\t\t\tn.Cfg.ShortName,\n616: \t\t\t\tIFaceName,\n617: \t\t\t\tIntfHelpMsg,\n618: \t\t\t)\n619: \t\t}\n620: \t}\n621: \n622: \treturn nil\n623: }\n624: \n625: func (n *iol) UpdateMgmtIntf(ctx context.Context) error {\n626: \t// L2 IOL images default to switchport mode, which rejects IP addresses.\n627: \tswitchportCmd := \"\"\n628: \tif n.isL2Node {\n629: \t\tswitchportCmd = \"no switchport\\r\"\n630: \t}\n631: \n632: \twaitCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, bootPromptTimeout)\n633: \tdefer cancel()\n634: \n635: \t// 1. Start streaming container logs\n636: \tlogReader, err := n.Runtime.StreamLogs(waitCtx, n.Cfg.LongName)\n637: \tif err != nil {\n638: \t\tlog.Warn(\"Skipping IOL mgmt interface update, cannot stream container logs\",\n639: \t\t\t\"node\", n.Cfg.ShortName, \"error\", err)\n640: \t\treturn nil\n641: \t}\n642: \tdefer logReader.Close()\n643: \n644: \t// Ticker to periodically send carriage returns (\\r) to wake up the serial console\n645: \tticker := time.NewTicker(2 * time.Second)\n646: \tdefer ticker.Stop()\n647: \n648: \t// Scanner to read the container log output line by line\n649: \tscanner := bufio.NewScanner(logReader)\n650: \n651: \t// Asynchronously send carriage returns since scanner.Scan() blocks\n652: \ttickCtx, stopTicker := context.WithCancel(waitCtx)\n653: \tdefer stopTicker()\n654: \ttickerDone := make(chan struct{})\n655: \n656: \tgo func() {\n657: \t\tdefer close(tickerDone)\n658: \t\tfor {\n659: \t\t\tselect {\n660: \t\t\tcase <-tickCtx.Done():\n661: \t\t\t\treturn\n662: \t\t\tcase <-ticker.C:\n663: \t\t\t\t_ = n.Runtime.WriteToStdinNoWait(tickCtx, n.Cfg.LongName, []byte(\"\\r\"))\n664: \t\t\t}\n665: \t\t}\n666: \t}()\n667: \n668: \tbootComplete := false\n669: \tfor scanner.Scan() {\n670: \t\t// Trim control characters and spaces from the log line\n671: \t\tline := strings.TrimSpace(scanner.Text())\n672: \t\tif line == \"\" {\n673: \t\t\tcontinue\n674: \t\t}\n675: \n676: \t\tlog.Debugf(\"[IOL Boot Log] %s\", line)\n677: \n678: \t\t// Match boot prompts (>, #, or initial config dialog)\n679: \t\tif strings.HasSuffix(line, \">\") ||\n680: \t\t\tstrings.HasSuffix(line, \"#\") ||\n681: \t\t\tstrings.Contains(line, \"initial configuration dialog?\") {\n682: \n683: \t\t\t// Ignore syslog messages containing '>'\n684: \t\t\tif strings.Contains(line, \"%\") {\n685: \t\t\t\tcontinue\n686: \t\t\t}\n687: \n688: \t\t\tlog.Infof(\"IOL boot prompt detected (%s). Proceeding with configuration.\", line)\n689: \t\t\tbootComplete = true\n690: \t\t\tbreak\n691: \t\t}\n692: \t}\n693: \n694: \tstopTicker()\n695: \t<-tickerDone\n696: \n697: \tif !bootComplete {\n698: \t\tif ctx.Err() != nil {\n699: \t\t\treturn ctx.Err()\n700: \t\t}\n701: \t\tif waitCtx.Err() != nil {\n702: \t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"node %q: timed out after %s waiting for IOL boot prompt\",\n703: \t\t\t\tn.Cfg.ShortName, bootPromptTimeout)\n704: \t\t}\n705: \t\tif err := scanner.Err(); error: %+v\", err)\n754: \t}\n755: \n756: \td, err := p.GetNetworkDriver()\n757: \tif err != nil {\n758: \t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"failed to fetch network driver from the platform; error: %+v\", err)\n759: \t}\n760: \n761: \terr = d.Open()\n762: \tif err != nil {\n763: \t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"failed to open driver; error: %+v\", err)\n764: \t}\n765: \n766: \tdefer d.Close()\n767: \n768: \t_, err = d.SendCommand(\"write memory\")\n769: \tif err != nil {\n770: \t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"failed to send command; error: %+v\", err)\n771: \t}\n772: \n773: \tlog.Infof(\n774: \t\t\"Successfully copied running configuration to startup configuration file for node: %q\\n\",\n775: \t\tn.Cfg.ShortName,\n776: \t)\n777: \treturn nil, nil\n778: }\n\n(End of file - total 778 lines)\n</content>",

        "text": "// Copyright 2020 Nokia\n// Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.\n// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause\n\npackage cisco_iol\n\nimport (\n\t\"bufio\"\n\t\"bytes\"\n\t\"context\"\n\t_ \"embed\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"path\"\n\t\"path/filepath\"\n\t\"regexp\"\n\t\"strconv\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"text/template\"\n\t\"time\"\n\n\t\"github.com/charmbracelet/log\"\n\t\"github.com/scrapli/scrapligo/driver/options\"\n\t\"github.com/scrapli/scrapligo/platform\"\n\tclabconstants \"github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants\"\n\tclablinks \"github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/links\"\n\tclabnodes \"github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/nodes\"\n\tclabtypes \"github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types\"\n\tclabutils \"github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils\"\n)\n\nconst (\n\ttypeIOL = \"iol\"\n\ttypeL2  = \"l2\"\n\n\tiol_workdir = \"/iol\"\n\n\tgenerateable     = true\n\tgenerateIfFormat = \"eth%d\"\n\n\tscrapliPlatformName = \"cisco_ios\"\n\tNapalmPlatformName  = \"ios\"\n\n\tbootPromptTimeout = 60 * time.Second\n)\n\nvar (\n\tkindNames          = []string{\"cisco_iol\"}\n\tdefaultCredentials = clabnodes.NewCredentials(\"admin\", \"admin\")\n\n\t//go:embed iol.cfg.tmpl\n\tcfgTemplate string\n\n\t// IntfRegexp with named capture groups for extracting slot and port.\n\tCapturingIntfRegexp = regexp.MustCompile(`^(?:e|Ethernet)\\s?(?P<slot>\\d+)/(?P<port>\\d+)$`)\n\t// ethX naming is the \"raw\" or \"default\" interface naming.\n\tDefaultIntfRegexp = regexp.MustCompile(`eth[1-9]\\d*$`)\n\t// Matches on any allowed/legal interface name.\n\tAllowedIntfRegexp = regexp.MustCompile(`(e|Ethernet)((0/[0-3])|([1-9]/[0-3]))$|eth[1-9]\\d*$`)\n\tIntfHelpMsg       = \"Interfaces should follow Ethernet<slot>/<port> or e<slot>/<port> naming convention, where <slot> is a number from 0-9 and <port> is a number from 0-3. You can also use ethX-based interface naming.\"\n\n\tvalidTypes = []string{typeIOL, typeL2}\n)\n\n// Register registers the node in the NodeRegistry.\nfunc Register(r *clabnodes.NodeRegistry) {\n\tgenerateNodeAttributes := clabnodes.NewGenerateNodeAttributes(generateable, generateIfFormat)\n\tplatformAttrs := &clabnodes.PlatformAttrs{\n\t\tScrapliPlatformName: scrapliPlatformName,\n\t\tNapalmPlatformName:  NapalmPlatformName,\n\t}\n\n\tnrea := clabnodes.NewNodeRegistryEntryAttributes(\n\t\tdefaultCredentials,\n\t\tgenerateNodeAttributes,\n\t\tplatformAttrs,\n\t).WithKindSpecificConfig(kindSpecificConfig)\n\n\tr.Register(kindNames, func() clabnodes.Node {\n\t\treturn new(iol)\n\t}, nrea)\n}\n\n// KindSpecificConfig is the cisco_iol kind-specific config, set as keys on the node definition.\ntype KindSpecificConfig struct {\n\t// PidOffset shifts the auto-assigned IOL PID, e.g. to keep IDs unique across labs.\n\tPidOffset *int `yaml:\"pid-offset,omitempty\" json:\"pid-offset,omitempty\"`\n\t// MgmtIntf is the management interface, e.g. Ethernet0/1. Defaults to Ethernet0/0.\n\tMgmtIntf string `yaml:\"mgmt-intf,omitempty\" json:\"mgmt-intf,omitempty\"`\n\t// BootstrapConfig replaces the default startup configuration with a file, or disables it\n\t// when set to \"none\".\n\tBootstrapConfig string `yaml:\"bootstrap-config,omitempty\" json:\"bootstrap-config,omitempty\"`\n}\n\nvar kindSpecificConfig clabnodes.KindSpecificConfigSpec[KindSpecificConfig]\n\ntype iol struct {\n\tclabnodes.DefaultNode\n\n\tisL2Node          bool\n\tPid               string\n\tnvramFile         string\n\tpartialStartupCfg string\n\tbootCfg           string\n\tinterfaces        []IOLInterface\n\tfirstBoot         bool\n\tbootstrapNone     bool\n\tbootstrapCfgFile  string\n\tmgmtIntf          string\n\tmgmtSlot          int\n\tmgmtPort          int\n\tmgmtLinuxIdx      int\n}\n\nfunc (n *iol) kindSpecificCfg() *KindSpecificConfig { return kindSpecificConfig.Of(n.Cfg) }\n\nfunc (n *iol) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {\n\t// Init DefaultNode\n\tn.DefaultNode = *clabnodes.NewDefaultNode(n)\n\tn.firstBoot = false\n\n\tn.Cfg = cfg\n\tfor _, o := range opts {\n\t\to(n)\n\t}\n\n\tnodeType := strings.ToLower(n.Cfg.NodeType)\n\n\tpid := n.Cfg.Index + 1 // n.Cfg.Index is zero-indexed, PID needs to be >= 1\n\tif off := n.kindSpecificCfg().PidOffset; off != nil {\n\t\tpid += *off\n\t}\n\n\tn.Pid = strconv.Itoa(pid)\n\n\tenv := map[string]string{\n\t\t\"IOL_PID\": n.Pid,\n\t}\n\n\tn.Cfg.Env = clabutils.MergeStringMaps(env, n.Cfg.Env)\n\n\t// check if user submitted node type is valid\n\tswitch nodeType {\n\tcase \"\":\n\t\tn.isL2Node = strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(path.Base(n.Cfg.Image)), \"l2\")\n\tcase typeIOL:\n\t\tn.isL2Node = false\n\tcase typeL2:\n\t\tn.isL2Node = true\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"invalid node type '%s'. Valid types are: %s\",\n\t\t\tn.Cfg.NodeType, strings.Join(validTypes, \", \"))\n\t}\n\n\tif err := n.parseMgmtIntf(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tn.nvramFile = fmt.Sprint(\"nvram_\", fmt.Sprintf(\"%05s\", n.Pid))\n\n\tn.Cfg.Binds = append(n.Cfg.Binds,\n\t\t// mount nvram so that config persists\n\t\tfmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, n.nvramFile), \":\", path.Join(iol_workdir, n.nvramFile)),\n\n\t\t// mount launch config\n\t\tfmt.Sprint(filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, \"boot_config.txt\"), \":/iol/config.txt\"),\n\n\t\t// mount IOYAP and NETMAP for interface mapping\n\t\tfmt.Sprint(filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, \"iouyap.ini\"), \":/iol/iouyap.ini\"),\n\t\tfmt.Sprint(filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, \"NETMAP\"), \":/iol/NETMAP\"),\n\t)\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// parseMgmtIntf parses the mgmt-intf kind-specific config key and normalizes it to\n// Ethernet<slot>/<port>;\n// empty means the default Ethernet0/0.\nfunc (n *iol) parseMgmtIntf() error {\n\tif v := n.kindSpecificCfg().MgmtIntf; v != \"\" {\n\t\tcaptureGroups, err := clabutils.GetRegexpCaptureGroups(CapturingIntfRegexp, v)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"invalid mgmt-intf %q: %w\\n%s\", v, err, IntfHelpMsg)\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tn.mgmtSlot, _ = strconv.Atoi(captureGroups[\"slot\"])\n\t\tn.mgmtPort, _ = strconv.Atoi(captureGroups[\"port\"])\n\n\t\tif n.mgmtSlot > 9 || n.mgmtPort > 3 {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\t\"invalid mgmt-intf %q: slot must be 0-9 and port must be 0-3\", v)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tn.mgmtIntf = fmt.Sprintf(\"Ethernet%d/%d\", n.mgmtSlot, n.mgmtPort)\n\tn.mgmtLinuxIdx = n.mgmtSlot*4 + n.mgmtPort\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// swapMgmtIdx swaps linux interface index 0 with the management interface's index,\n// so Ethernet0/0 takes the index a relocated management interface vacated.\nfunc (n *iol) swapMgmtIdx(idx int) int {\n\tswitch idx {\n\tcase 0:\n\t\treturn n.mgmtLinuxIdx\n\tcase n.mgmtLinuxIdx:\n\t\treturn 0\n\t}\n\n\treturn idx\n}\n\n// iolPortForLinuxIdx returns the IOL slot/port backed by linux interface index idx.\nfunc (n *iol) iolPortForLinuxIdx(idx int) (slot, port int) {\n\tmapped := n.swapMgmtIdx(idx)\n\treturn mapped / 4, mapped % 4\n}\n\n// ensureNumSlotsEnv exports CLAB_IOL_NUM_SLOTS when the management interface is\n// relocated, so that its slot exists even when no link lands in it.\nfunc (n *iol) ensureNumSlotsEnv() {\n\tif n.mgmtLinuxIdx == 0 || n.Cfg.Env[\"CLAB_IOL_NUM_SLOTS\"] != \"\" {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tintfIdxRegexp := regexp.MustCompile(`\\d+`)\n\tneeded := n.mgmtSlot + 1\n\n\tfor _, ep := range n.Endpoints {\n\t\tx, _ := strconv.Atoi(intfIdxRegexp.FindString(ep.GetIfaceName()))\n\t\tif slot, _ := n.iolPortForLinuxIdx(x); slot+1 > needed {\n\t\t\tneeded = slot + 1\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tn.Cfg.Env[\"CLAB_IOL_NUM_SLOTS\"] = strconv.Itoa(needed)\n}\n\nfunc (n *iol) PreDeploy(ctx context.Context, params *clabnodes.PreDeployParams) error {\n\tclabutils.CreateDirectory(n.Cfg.LabDir, clabconstants.PermissionsOpen)\n\n\tif v := n.kindSpecificCfg().BootstrapConfig; v != \"\" {\n\t\tswitch p := clabutils.ResolvePath(v, params.TopoPaths.TopologyFileDir()); {\n\t\tcase strings.EqualFold(v, \"none\"):\n\t\t\tn.bootstrapNone = true\n\t\tcase clabutils.FileExists(p):\n\t\t\tn.bootstrapCfgFile = p\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"bootstrap-config file %q does not exist\", p)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t_, err := n.LoadOrGenerateCertificate(params.Cert, params.TopologyName)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tn.ensureNumSlotsEnv()\n\n\treturn n.CreateIOLFiles(ctx)\n}\n\nfunc (n *iol) PostDeploy(ctx context.Context, _ *clabnodes.PostDeployParams) error {\n\tlog.Infof(\"Running postdeploy actions for Cisco IOL '%s' node\", n.Cfg.ShortName)\n\n\tn.disableMgmtTxOffload(ctx)\n\n\tif err := n.GenBootConfig(ctx); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to generate boot config: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\n\t// Must update mgmt IP if not first boot, unless the node boots without a baseline config\n\tif !n.firstBoot && !n.bootstrapNone {\n\t\treturn n.UpdateMgmtIntf(ctx)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// Start re-applies the mgmt veth TX offload fix after a stop/start cycle. The runtime\n// recreates the mgmt veth (it is never parked), so its offload settings reset to defaults.\n// See disableMgmtTxOffload for why IOL cannot function with it enabled.\nfunc (n *iol) Start(ctx context.Context) error {\n\tif err := n.DefaultNode.Start(ctx); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\t// DefaultNode.Start no-ops for root-ns and auto-remove nodes; skip the offload fix\n\t// for them as well, as there is no container mgmt veth to adjust.\n\tif n.ShouldSkipLifecycle() {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tn.disableMgmtTxOffload(ctx)\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// disableMgmtTxOffload disables TX checksum offload on the host NS veth for the mgmt interface.\n// iouyap bridges IOL interfaces over packet sockets; frames carrying an offloaded\n// (CHECKSUM_PARTIAL) checksum reach the IOL process with an incomplete checksum, which its\n// TCP/IP stack drops, breaking TCP/UDP connectivity.\nfunc (n *iol) disableMgmtTxOffload(ctx context.Context) {\n\tif n.Runtime.Mgmt().Driver == clabtypes.MgmtDriverMacvlan {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tvar peerIfIndex int\n\terr := n.ExecFunction(ctx, clabutils.VethPeerIndex(\"eth0\", &peerIfIndex))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tlog.Warn(\"Failed to get veth peer index for IOL mgmt interface\",\n\t\t\t\"node\", n.Cfg.ShortName,\n\t\t\t\"error\", err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tif err := clabutils.DisableTxOffloadByIndex(peerIfIndex); err != nil {\n\t\tlog.Warn(\"Failed to disable TX checksum offload on IOL mgmt host veth\",\n\t\t\t\"node\", n.Cfg.ShortName,\n\t\t\t\"error\", err)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (n *iol) CreateIOLFiles(ctx context.Context) error {\n\t// If NVRAM already exists, don't need to create\n\t// otherwise saved configs in NVRAM are overwritten.\n\tif !clabutils.FileExists(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, n.nvramFile)) {\n\t\t// create nvram file\n\t\tclabutils.CreateFile(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, n.nvramFile), \"\")\n\t\tn.firstBoot = true\n\t}\n\n\t// create these files so the bind monut doesn't automatically\n\t// make folders.\n\tclabutils.CreateFile(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, \"boot_config.txt\"), \"\")\n\n\treturn n.GenInterfaceConfig(ctx)\n}\n\n// Generate interfaces configuration for IOL (and iouyap/netmap).\nfunc (n *iol) GenInterfaceConfig(_ context.Context) error {\n\t// add 'boilerplate' to NETMAP and iouyap.ini for the management port\n\tiouyapData := fmt.Sprintf(\n\t\t\"[default]\\nbase_port = 49000\\nnetmap = /iol/NETMAP\\n[513:%d/%d]\\neth_dev = eth0\\n\",\n\t\tn.mgmtSlot,\n\t\tn.mgmtPort,\n\t)\n\tnetmapdata := fmt.Sprintf(\n\t\t\"%s:%d/%d 513:%d/%d\\n\",\n\t\tn.Pid,\n\t\tn.mgmtSlot,\n\t\tn.mgmtPort,\n\t\tn.mgmtSlot,\n\t\tn.mgmtPort,\n\t)\n\n\tslot, port := 0, 0\n\n\t// Regexp to pull number out of linux'ethX' interface naming\n\tIntfRegExpr := regexp.MustCompile(`\\d+`)\n\n\tfor _, intf := range n.Endpoints {\n\t\t// get numeric interface number and cast to int\n\t\tx, _ := strconv.Atoi(IntfRegExpr.FindString(intf.GetIfaceName()))\n\n\t\t// Interface naming is Ethernet{slot}/{port}. Each slot contains max 4 ports\n\t\tslot, port = n.iolPortForLinuxIdx(x)\n\n\t\t// append data to write to NETMAP and IOUYAP files\n\t\tiouyapData += fmt.Sprintf(\"[513:%d/%d]\\neth_dev = %s\\n\", slot, port, intf.GetIfaceName())\n\t\tnetmapdata += fmt.Sprintf(\"%s:%d/%d 513:%d/%d\\n\", n.Pid, slot, port, slot, port)\n\n\t\t// populate template array for config\n\t\tipv4Addr := \"\"\n\t\tipv4Mask := \"\"\n\t\tv4Prefix := intf.GetIPv4Addr()\n\t\tipv6Addr := \"\"\n\n\t\tif v4Prefix.IsValid() {\n\t\t\tipv4Addr = v4Prefix.Addr().String()\n\t\t\tipv4Mask = clabutils.CIDRToDDN(v4Prefix.Bits())\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif a := intf.GetIPv6Addr(); a.IsValid() {\n\t\t\tipv6Addr = a.String()\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tn.interfaces = append(n.interfaces,\n\t\t\tIOLInterface{\n\t\t\t\tIfaceName: intf.GetIfaceName(),\n\t\t\t\tIfaceIdx:  x,\n\t\t\t\tSlot:      slot,\n\t\t\t\tPort:      port,\n\t\t\t\tIPv4Addr:  ipv4Addr,\n\t\t\t\tIPv4Mask:  ipv4Mask,\n\t\t\t\tIPv6Addr:  ipv6Addr,\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t)\n\t}\n\n\t// create IOUYAP and NETMAP file for interface mappings\n\terr := clabutils.CreateFile(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, \"iouyap.ini\"), iouyapData)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\terr = clabutils.CreateFile(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, \"NETMAP\"), netmapdata)\n\n\treturn err\n}\n\nfunc (n *iol) GenBootConfig(_ context.Context) error {\n\tn.bootCfg = cfgTemplate\n\n\tswitch {\n\tcase n.bootstrapNone:\n\t\tn.bootCfg = \"{{ .PartialCfg }}\"\n\tcase n.bootstrapCfgFile != \"\":\n\t\tcfg, err := os.ReadFile(n.bootstrapCfgFile)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tn.bootCfg = string(cfg)\n\t}\n\n\tif n.Cfg.StartupConfig != \"\" {\n\t\tcfg, err := os.ReadFile(n.Cfg.StartupConfig)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif clabutils.IsPartialConfigFile(n.Cfg.StartupConfig) {\n\t\t\tn.partialStartupCfg = string(cfg)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tn.bootCfg = string(cfg)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// create startup config template\n\ttpl := IOLTemplateData{\n\t\tHostname:           n.Cfg.ShortName,\n\t\tIsL2Node:           n.isL2Node,\n\t\tMgmtIntf:           n.mgmtIntf,\n\t\tMgmtIPv4Addr:       n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4Address,\n\t\tMgmtIPv4SubnetMask: clabutils.CIDRToDDN(n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4PrefixLength),\n\t\tMgmtIPv4GW:         n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4Gateway,\n\t\tMgmtIPv6Addr:       n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6Address,\n\t\tMgmtIPv6PrefixLen:  n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6PrefixLength,\n\t\tMgmtIPv6GW:         n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6Gateway,\n\t\tDataIFaces:         n.interfaces,\n\t}\n\n\t// render the partial startup config so template variables work in partials too\n\tif n.partialStartupCfg != \"\" {\n\t\tpartialTpl, err := template.New(\"clab-iol-partial-config\").Funcs(\n\t\t\tclabutils.CreateFuncs()).Parse(n.partialStartupCfg)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tbuf := new(bytes.Buffer)\n\t\tif err := partialTpl.Execute(buf, tpl); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\ttpl.PartialCfg = buf.String()\n\t}\n\n\tIOLCfgTpl, err := template.New(\"clab-iol-default-config\").Funcs(\n\t\tclabutils.CreateFuncs()).Parse(n.bootCfg)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\t// generate the config\n\tbuf := new(bytes.Buffer)\n\terr = IOLCfgTpl.Execute(buf, tpl)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\treturn clabutils.CreateFile(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, \"boot_config.txt\"), buf.String())\n}\n\ntype IOLTemplateData struct {\n\tHostname           string\n\tIsL2Node           bool\n\tMgmtIntf           string\n\tMgmtIPv4Addr       string\n\tMgmtIPv4SubnetMask string\n\tMgmtIPv4GW         string\n\tMgmtIPv6Addr       string\n\tMgmtIPv6PrefixLen  int\n\tMgmtIPv6GW         string\n\tDataIFaces         []IOLInterface\n\tPartialCfg         string\n}\n\n// IOLInterface struct stores mapping info between\n// IOL interface name and linux container interface.\ntype IOLInterface struct {\n\tIfaceName string\n\tIfaceIdx  int\n\tSlot      int\n\tPort      int\n\tIPv4Addr  string\n\tIPv4Mask  string\n\tIPv6Addr  string\n}\n\nfunc (n *iol) GetMappedInterfaceName(ifName string) (string, error) {\n\tcaptureGroups, err := clabutils.GetRegexpCaptureGroups(CapturingIntfRegexp, ifName)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\", err\n\t}\n\n\tindexGroups := []string{\"slot\", \"port\"}\n\tparsedIndices := make(map[string]int)\n\tfoundIndices := make(map[string]bool)\n\n\tfor _, indexKey := range indexGroups {\n\t\tif index, found := captureGroups[indexKey]; found && index != \"\" {\n\t\t\tfoundIndices[indexKey] = true\n\t\t\tparsedIndices[indexKey], err = strconv.Atoi(index)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\t\t\"%q parsed %s index %q could not be cast to an integer\",\n\t\t\t\t\tifName,\n\t\t\t\t\tindexKey,\n\t\t\t\t\tindex,\n\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif parsedIndices[indexKey] < 0 {\n\t\t\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\t\t\"%q parsed %q index %q does not match requirement >= 0\",\n\t\t\t\t\tifName,\n\t\t\t\t\tindexKey,\n\t\t\t\t\tindex,\n\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tfoundIndices[indexKey] = false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// return an ethX interface name. Slots are in 'groups' of 4 interfaces each\n\tif foundIndices[\"slot\"] && foundIndices[\"port\"] {\n\t\tidx := n.swapMgmtIdx((parsedIndices[\"slot\"] * 4) + parsedIndices[\"port\"])\n\t\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"eth%d\", idx), nil\n\t} else {\n\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"%q missing slot or port index\", ifName)\n\t}\n}\n\n// AddEndpoint override maps the endpoint name to an ethX-based naming where necessary, before\n// adding it to the node endpoints. Returns an error if the mapping goes wrong or if the\n// interface name is NOT allowed.\nfunc (n *iol) AddEndpoint(e clablinks.Endpoint) error {\n\tendpointName := e.GetIfaceName()\n\tvar IFaceName, IFaceAlias string\n\n\tIFaceName = endpointName\n\n\tif !(DefaultIntfRegexp.MatchString(endpointName)) &&\n\t\tAllowedIntfRegexp.MatchString(endpointName) {\n\t\tlog.Debugf(\"%s: %s needs mapping\", n.Cfg.ShortName, endpointName)\n\t\tmappedName, err := n.GetMappedInterfaceName(endpointName)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\t\"%q interface name %q could not be mapped to an ethX-based interface name: %w\\n%s\",\n\t\t\t\tn.Cfg.ShortName,\n\t\t\t\te.GetIfaceName(),\n\t\t\t\terr,\n\t\t\t\tIntfHelpMsg,\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t}\n\t\tlog.Debugf(\n\t\t\t\"Interface Mapping: Mapping interface %q (ifAlias) to %q (ifName)\",\n\t\t\tendpointName,\n\t\t\tmappedName,\n\t\t)\n\t\tIFaceName = mappedName\n\t\tIFaceAlias = endpointName\n\t}\n\n\te.SetIfaceName(IFaceName)\n\t// should be nil if ethX naming is used.\n\te.SetIfaceAlias(IFaceAlias)\n\tn.Endpoints = append(n.Endpoints, e)\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (n *iol) CheckInterfaceName() error {\n\terr := n.CheckInterfaceOverlap()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tfor _, e := range n.Endpoints {\n\t\tIFaceName := e.GetIfaceName()\n\t\t// eth0 always backs the management interface\n\t\tif IFaceName == \"eth0\" {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\t\"IOL Node: %q. Management interface %s (eth0) is not allowed\",\n\t\t\t\tn.Cfg.ShortName,\n\t\t\t\tn.mgmtIntf,\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif !DefaultIntfRegexp.MatchString(IFaceName) {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\t\"IOL Node %q has an interface named %q which doesn't match the required pattern. %s\",\n\t\t\t\tn.Cfg.ShortName,\n\t\t\t\tIFaceName,\n\t\t\t\tIntfHelpMsg,\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (n *iol) UpdateMgmtIntf(ctx context.Context) error {\n\t// L2 IOL images default to switchport mode, which rejects IP addresses.\n\tswitchportCmd := \"\"\n\tif n.isL2Node {\n\t\tswitchportCmd = \"no switchport\\r\"\n\t}\n\n\twaitCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, bootPromptTimeout)\n\tdefer cancel()\n\n\t// 1. 23: 	generateIfFormat = "eth%d"
24: )
25: 
26: var kindnames = []string{"linux"}
27: 
28: // Register registers the node in the NodeRegistry.
29: func Register(r *clabnodes.NodeRegistry) {
30: 	generateNodeAttributes := clabnodes.NewGenerateNodeAttributes(generateable, generateIfFormat)
31: 	nrea := clabnodes.NewNodeRegistryEntryAttributes(nil, generateNodeAttributes, nil)
32: 
33: 	r.Register(kindnames, func() clabnodes.Node {
34: 		return new(linux)
35: 	}, nrea)
36: }
37: 
38: type linux struct {
39: 	clabnodes.DefaultNode
40: }
41: 
42: func (*linux) LinkApplyMode(context.Context) clabnodes.LinkApplyMode {
43: 	return clabnodes.LinkApplyModeLive
44: }
45: 
46: func (n *linux) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {
47: 	// Init DefaultNode
48: 	n.DefaultNode = *clabnodes.NewDefaultNode(n)
49: 	n.Cfg = cfg
50: 
51: 	n.StopSignal = clabtypes.SIGKILL
52: 
53: 	// linux kind uses `always` as a default restart policy
54: 	// since often they run auxiliary services that might fail because
55: 	// of the wrong configuration or other reasons.
56: 	// Usually we want those services to automatically restart.
57: 	if n.Cfg.RestartPolicy == "" {
58: 		n.Cfg.RestartPolicy = "always"
59: 	}
60: 
61: 	for _, o := range opts {
62: 		o(n)
63: 	}
64: 
65: 	// make ipv6 enabled on all linux node interfaces
66: 	// but not for the nodes with host network mode, as this is not supported on gh action runners
67: 	if cfg.Sysctls != nil && n.Config().NetworkMode != "host" {
68: 		cfg.Sysctls["net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6"] = "0"
69: 	}
70: 
71: 	return nil
72: }
73: 
74: func (n *linux) Deploy(ctx context.Context, _ *clabnodes.DeployParams) error {
75: 	// Set the "CLAB_INTFS" variable to the number of interfaces
76: 	// Which is required by vrnetlab to determine if all configured interfaces are present
77: 	// such that the internal VM can be started with these interfaces assigned.
78: 	n.Config().Env[clabconstants.ClabEnvIntfs] = strconv.Itoa(len(n.GetEndpoints()))
79: 
80: 	cID, err := n.Runtime.CreateContainer(ctx, n.Cfg)
81: 	if err != nil {
82: 		return err
83: 	}
84: 	_, err = n.Runtime.StartContainer(ctx, cID, n)
85: 
86: 	n.SetState(clabnodesstate.Deployed)
87: 
88: 	return err
89: }

91: func (n *linux) PostDeploy(ctx context.Context, _ *clabnodes.PostDeployParams) error {
92: 	log.Debugf("Running postdeploy actions for Linux '%s' node", n.Cfg.ShortName)
93: 
94: 	n.disableEth0TxOffload(ctx)
95: 
96: 	return nil
97: }
98: 
99: // Start re-applies the eth0 TX offload fix after a stop/start cycle. The runtime recreates
100: // the mgmt veth (it is never parked), so its offload settings reset to defaults.
101: // See disableEth0TxOffload for why TX offload must stay disabled on eth0.
102: func (n *linux) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
103: 	if err := n.DefaultNode.Start(ctx); err != nil {
104: 		return err
105: 	}
106: 
107: 	// DefaultNode.Start no-ops for root-ns and auto-remove nodes; skip the offload fix
108: 	// for them as well, as there is no container netns to adjust.
109: 	if n.ShouldSkipLifecycle() {
110: 		return nil
111: 	}
112: 
113: 	n.disableEth0TxOffload(ctx)
114: 
115: 	return nil
116: }
117: 
118: // disableEth0TxOffload disables TX checksum offload on the container's eth0 interface.
119: // Frames crossing the veth with an offloaded (CHECKSUM_PARTIAL) checksum break consumers
120: // that bridge or capture traffic on that interface, so the setting is (re-)applied on
121: // deploy and after every stop/start cycle, when the runtime recreates the mgmt veth.
122: func (n *linux) disableEth0TxOffload(ctx context.Context) {
123: 	err := n.ExecFunction(ctx, clabutils.NSEthtoolTXOff(n.GetShortName(), "eth0"))
124: 	if err != nil {
125: 		log.Error(err)
126: 	}
127: }
128: 
129: func (n *linux) GetImages(_ context.Context) map[string]string {
130: 	images := make(map[string]string)
131: 	images[clabnodes.ImageKey] = n.Cfg.Image
132: 
133: 	return images
134: }
135: 
136: // CheckInterfaceName allows any interface name for linux nodes, but checks
137: // if eth0 is only used with network-mode=none.
138: func (n *linux) CheckInterfaceName() error {
139: 	nm := strings.ToLower(n.Cfg.NetworkMode)
140: 	for _, e := range n.Endpoints {
141: 		if e.GetIfaceName() == "eth0" && nm != "none" {
142: 			return fmt.Errorf(
143: 				"eth0 interface name is not allowed for %s node when network mode is not set to none",
144: 				n.Cfg.ShortName,
145: 			)
146: 		}
147: 	}
148: 	return nil
149: }

{\n\t\tcfg.Sysctls[\"net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6\"] = \"0\"\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (n *linux) Deploy(ctx context.Context, _ *clabnodes.DeployParams) error {\n\t// Set the \"CLAB_INTFS\" variable to the number of interfaces\n\t// Which is required by vrnetlab to determine if all configured interfaces are present\n\t// such that the internal VM can be started with these interfaces assigned.\n\tn.Config().Env[clabconstants.ClabEnvIntfs] = strconv.Itoa(len(n.GetEndpoints()))\n\n\tcID, err := n.Runtime.CreateContainer(ctx, n.Cfg)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\t_, err = n.Runtime.StartContainer(ctx, cID, n)\n\n\tn.SetState(clabnodesstate.Deployed)\n\n\treturn err\n}\n\nfunc (n *linux) PostDeploy(ctx context.Context, _ *clabnodes.PostDeployParams) error {\n\tlog.Debugf(\"Running postdeploy actions for Linux '%s' node\", n.Cfg.ShortName)\n\n\tn.disableEth0TxOffload(ctx)\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// Start re-applies the eth0 TX offload fix after a stop/start cycle. The runtime recreates\n// the mgmt veth (it is never parked), so its offload settings reset to defaults.\n// See disableEth0TxOffload for why TX offload must stay disabled on eth0.\nfunc (n *linux) Start(ctx context.Context) error {\n\tif err := n.DefaultNode.Start(ctx); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\t// DefaultNode.Start no-ops for root-ns and auto-remove nodes; skip the offload fix\n\t// for them as well, as there is no container netns to adjust.\n\tif n.ShouldSkipLifecycle() {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tn.disableEth0TxOffload(ctx)\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// disableEth0TxOffload disables TX checksum offload on the container's eth0 interface.\n// Frames crossing the veth with an offloaded (CHECKSUM_PARTIAL) checksum break consumers\n// that bridge or capture traffic on that interface, so the setting is (re-)applied on\n// deploy and after every stop/start cycle, when the runtime recreates the mgmt veth.\nfunc (n *linux) disableEth0TxOffload(ctx context.Context) {\n\terr := n.ExecFunction(ctx, clabutils.NSEthtoolTXOff(n.GetShortName(), \"eth0\"))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tlog.Error(err)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (n *linux) GetImages(_ context.Context) map[string]string {\n\timages := make(map[string]string)\n\timages[clabnodes.ImageKey] = n.Cfg.Image\n\n\treturn images\n}\n\n// CheckInterfaceName allows any interface name for linux nodes, but checks\n// if eth0 is only used with network-mode=none.\nfunc (n *linux) CheckInterfaceName() error {\n\tnm := strings.ToLower(n.Cfg.NetworkMode)\n\tfor _, e := range n.Endpoints {\n\t\tif e.GetIfaceName() == \"eth0\" && nm != \"none\" {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\t\"eth0 interface name is not allowed for %s node when network mode is not set to none\",\n\t\t\t\tn.Cfg.ShortName,\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}",

5: package utils

22: )
23: 
24: // IFReqData linux/if.h 'struct ifreq'.
25: type IFReqData struct {
26: 	Name [IFNAMSIZ]byte
27: 	Data uintptr
28: }
29: 
30: // EthtoolValue linux/ethtool.h 'struct ethtool_value'.
31: type EthtoolValue struct {
32: 	Cmd  uint32
33: 	Data uint32
34: }
35: 
36: func ioctlEthtool(fd int, argp uintptr) error {
37: 	_, _, errno := syscall.RawSyscall(syscall.SYS_IOCTL, uintptr(fd), uintptr(SIOCETHTOOL), argp)
38: 	if errno != 0 {
39: 		return errno
40: 	}
41: 	return nil
42: }
43: 
44: // NSEthtoolTXOff EthtoolTXOff wrapper that can be handed straight to Node.ExecFunc().
45: func NSEthtoolTXOff(cntName, ifaceName string) func(ns.NetNS) error {
46: 	return func(ns.NetNS) error {
47: 		// disabling offload on given interface
48: 		err := EthtoolTXOff(ifaceName)
49: 		if err != nil {
50: 			log.Infof(
51: 				"failed to disable TX checksum offload for %s interface for %s container",
52: 				ifaceName,
53: 				cntName,
54: 			)
55: 		}
56: 		return nil
57: 	}
58: }
59: 
60: // EthtoolTXOff disables TX checksum offload on specified interface.
61: func EthtoolTXOff(name string) error {
62: 	if len(name)+1 > IFNAMSIZ {
63: 		return fmt.Errorf("name too long")
64: 	}
65: 
66: 	socket, err := syscall.Socket(syscall.AF_INET, syscall.SOCK_DGRAM, 0)
67: 	if err != nil {
68: 		return err
69: 	}
70: 	defer syscall.Close(socket)
71: 
72: 	// Request current value
73: 	value := EthtoolValue{Cmd: ETHTOOL_GTXCSUM}
74: 	request := IFReqData{Data: uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(&value))} // skipcq: GSC-G103
75: 	copy(request.Name[:], name)
76: 
77: 	if err := ioctlEthtool(
78: 		socket,
79: 		uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(&request)),
80: 	); err != nil { // skipcq: GSC-G103
81: 		return err
82: 	}
83: 	if value.Data == 0 { // if already off, don't try to change
84: 		return nil
85: 	}
86: 
87: 	value = EthtoolValue{ETHTOOL_STXCSUM, 0}
88: 	return ioctlEthtool(socket, uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(&request))) // skipcq: GSC-G103
89: }
90: 
91: // VethPeerIndex gets the interface index of the veth peer for
92: // the given interface name in the container.
93: func VethPeerIndex(ifaceName string, peerIndex *int) func(ns.NetNS) error {
94: 	return func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
95: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(ifaceName)
96: 		if err != nil {
97: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to find %s in container: %w", ifaceName, err)
98: 		}
99: 
100: 		// confirm it's a veth.
101: 		veth, ok := link.(*netlink.Veth)
102: 		if !ok {
103: 			return fmt.Errorf("%s is not a veth interface", ifaceName)
104: 		}
105: 
106: 		*peerIndex, err = netlink.VethPeerIndex(veth)
107: 		if err != nil {
108: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to get peer interface index: %w", err)
109: 		}
110: 
111: 		return nil
112: 	}
113: }
114: 
115: // DisableTxOffloadByIndex disables TX checksum offload on an interface by its index.
116: func DisableTxOffloadByIndex(index int) error {
117: 	link, err := netlink.LinkByIndex(index)
118: 	if err != nil {
119: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to find interface with index %d: %w", index, err)
120: 	}
121: 
122: 	ifaceName := link.Attrs().Name
123: 	log.Debugf("Disabling TX offload on interface %s (index %d)", ifaceName, index)
124: 
125: 	if err := EthtoolTXOff(ifaceName); err != nil {
126: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to disable TX offload on %s: %w", ifaceName, err)
127: 	}
128: 
129: 	log.Debug("Successfully disabled TX offload on the host ns interface", "interface", ifaceName)
130: 
131: 	return nil
132: }

213: // GetNSPath retrieves the nodes nspath.
214: func (d *DefaultNode) GetNSPath(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
215: 	var err error
216: 	nsp := ""
217: 
218: 	if d.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased {
219: 		netns, err := ns.GetCurrentNS()
220: 		if err != nil {
221: 			return "", err
222: 		}
223: 		nsp = netns.Path()
224: 	}
225: 	if nsp == "" {
226: 		nsp, err = d.Runtime.GetNSPath(ctx, d.OverwriteNode.GetContainerName())
227: 		if err != nil {
228: 			log.Errorf("Unable to determine NetNS Path for node %s: %v", d.Cfg.ShortName, err)
229: 			return "", err
230: 		}
231: 	}
232: 
233: 	return nsp, err
234: }

236: // ShouldSkipLifecycle reports whether lifecycle operations should no-op for this node.
237: func (d *DefaultNode) ShouldSkipLifecycle() bool {
238: 	return d.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased || d.Cfg.AutoRemove
239: }

241: // LinkApplyMode returns the conservative default for node kinds that do not

244: 	if d.Cfg != nil && (d.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased || d.Cfg.SkipUniquenessCheck) {
